grapes.name: Albarino
characteristics: Primary flavours: citrus (lemon, grapefruit), stone fruit (peach, apricot)
Oaked: no, most commonly unoaked and drunk young; sometimes small lees contact for body/complexity

grapes.name: Barbera
characteristics: Primary flavours: red fruit (red cherries, red plums), sometimes black pepper
Oaked: many unoaked and fruity; some oak-matured for complexity
Style: generally drinks younger and has shorter ageing potential than Nebbiolo

grapes.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
characteristics: Primary flavours: black fruit (blackcurrant, black cherry), herbal (mint) or herbaceous (green bell pepper/capsicum); cooked in warm climates
Oaked: often, matured in oak barrels for months to years; new oak adds smoke, vanilla, cloves, cedar
Tertiary flavours: dried fruits, earth, forest floor

grapes.name: Carmenere
characteristics: Climate: needs a long, sunny growing season
Primary flavours (underripe): herbaceous, green bell pepper/capsicum, tomato leaf
Oaked: often, softens tannins and adds coffee/chocolate flavours

grapes.name: Chardonnay
characteristics: Cool-climate style: high acidity, light to medium body, green fruit (apple, pear), citrus (lemon), wet stones
Moderate-climate style: medium to high acidity, medium to full body, lemon, stone fruit (peach), sometimes tropical (melon)
Warm-climate style: full body, medium acidity, stone fruit (peach), tropical fruit (pineapple, banana)
Secondary flavours: malolactic conversion (butter, cream), lees contact (bread, biscuit), oak (smoke, vanilla, coconut) - all optional
Oaked: often, though unoaked/unwooded styles also made

grapes.name: Chenin Blanc
characteristics: Primary flavours: green fruit (apple), citrus (lemon) through stone fruit (peach) and tropical fruit (pineapple, mango) depending on ripeness
Style: dry through sweet; suited to late harvest and botrytis/noble rot
Oaked: both oaked and unoaked styles produced

grapes.name: Cortese
characteristics: Primary flavours: floral (blossom), green fruit (apple, pear), citrus (lemon)
Oaked: no, fermented in inert vessels

grapes.name: Corvina
characteristics: Primary flavours: red fruit (red cherry, red plum)
Oaked: basic Valpolicella matured in new oak
Style: typically the dominant grape in a blend with other local varieties

grapes.name: Fiano
characteristics: Primary flavours: stone fruit (peach), tropical fruit (melon, mango)
Secondary flavours: lees contact (bread, biscuit) or oak (smoke) in some examples
Oaked: some examples, though most fermented in inert vessels

grapes.name: Furmint
characteristics: Colour: amber (Tokaji Aszu, from oak ageing)
Primary/tertiary flavours (Tokaji Aszu): fresh and dried stone fruit (apricot), citrus, oak (vanilla, smoke), tertiary (dried fruit, caramel, nuts)
Oaked: yes, traditionally significant oak ageing for Tokaji Aszu
Style: dry, medium and sweet produced; most famous is sweet (Tokaji Aszu)

grapes.name: Gamay
characteristics: Primary flavours: red fruit (raspberry, red cherry, red plum)
Oaked: no, made in inert vessels, rarely oak aromas
Style: usually light to medium body, most intended for immediate consumption

grapes.name: Garganega
characteristics: Primary flavours: green fruit (apple, pear), citrus (lemon), stone fruit (peach)
Oaked: no, fermented in inert vessels
Tertiary flavours: honey, almonds (best examples of Soave Classico)

grapes.name: Gewurztraminer
characteristics: Primary flavours: floral (rose), stone fruit (peach, apricot), tropical fruit (lychee)
Oaked: no, typically unoaked to preserve floral aromas

grapes.name: Grenache/Garnacha
characteristics: Primary flavours: red fruit (strawberry, red plum, red cherry), sometimes spice (white pepper, liquorice)
Oaked: simple wines usually unoaked; very good/outstanding often barrel matured
Tertiary flavours: earth, meat, dried fruit
Also widely used for rose (short maceration method), dry to medium sweetness

grapes.name: Malbec
characteristics: Primary flavours: black fruit (blackberry, black plum)
Oaked: new oak common, adds softness and clove/vanilla flavours

grapes.name: Merlot
characteristics: Primary flavours (just-ripe): light to medium body, red fruit (strawberry, red plum), herbaceous (green bell pepper/capsicum)
Primary flavours (riper): medium to full body, cooked black fruit (blackberry, black plum)
Oaked: both oaked and unoaked styles made

grapes.name: Montepulciano
characteristics: Primary flavours: black fruit (black plum, black cherry)
Oaked: more concentrated wines matured briefly in oak; much is simple and unoaked for early drinking

grapes.name: Nebbiolo
characteristics: Primary flavours: red fruit (red cherry, red plum), dried herbs, sometimes floral (rose, violet)
Oaked: often, extended maturation in old or new oak barrels

grapes.name: Pinot Grigio/Pinot Gris
characteristics: Style 1 (Pinot Grigio, high yield/early harvest): dry, light body, medium to high acidity, simple pear and lemon flavours
Style 2 (riper, controlled yield/delayed harvest): full body, medium acidity, pronounced lemon, stone fruit (peach) and tropical fruit (mango, banana); can be off-dry or medium sweetness
Oaked: no, typically fermented in inert vessels
Tertiary flavours: ginger, honey (fuller-bodied style, with bottle age)

grapes.name: Pinot Noir
characteristics: Primary flavours: red fruit, from fresh to cooked depending on ripeness

grapes.name: Pinotage
characteristics: Style: ranges fruity medium-bodied to powerful full-bodied
Primary flavours: red fruit (strawberry, raspberry, red cherry), or red/black fruit (red plum, blackberry) in fuller styles

grapes.name: Riesling
characteristics: Style: dry to sweet, light to full body
Primary flavours (just-ripe): green fruit (apple, pear), citrus (lemon, lime), floral (blossom)
Primary flavours (extra-ripe): stone fruit (peach, apricot), tropical fruit (mango, pineapple), dried fruit (dried apricot)
Oaked: no, typically fermented in inert vessels

grapes.name: Sangiovese
characteristics: Primary flavours: red fruit (red cherries, red plums), dried herbs
Oaked: often, softens tannins and adds cloves/cedar

grapes.name: Sauvignon Blanc
characteristics: Primary flavours (herbaceous): grass, green bell pepper/capsicum, asparagus
Primary flavours (fruit, by ripeness): green fruit (apple, gooseberry), citrus (grapefruit), wet stones, through to riper stone fruit (peach) and tropical fruit (passion fruit)
Oaked: usually unoaked; if oaked, labelled 'barrel aged'

grapes.name: Semillon/Sémillon
characteristics: Tertiary flavours: dried fruit, nuts, honey
Oaked: yes for very good/outstanding examples; Hunter Valley style uses inert vessels (unoaked)

grapes.name: Syrah/Shiraz
characteristics: Moderate-climate style (Syrah): medium body, fresh black fruit (black cherry, blackberry), herbal notes, black pepper
Warm-climate style (Shiraz): full body, high alcohol, cooked black fruit, liquorice
Oaked: common, softens tannins and adds smoke/spice
Tertiary flavours: dried fruit, leather, meat, earth

grapes.name: Tempranillo
characteristics: Primary flavours: red fruit (strawberry, red cherry), black fruit (blackberry, black plum)
Oaked: traditionally matured in small new-oak barrels; often also bottle-aged before release
Tertiary flavours: mushroom, leather, dried fruit

grapes.name: Verdicchio
characteristics: Primary flavours: green fruit (apple, pear), citrus (lemon), herbal (fennel)

grapes.name: Viognier
characteristics: Primary flavours: floral (blossom), stone fruit (peach, apricot)
Oaked: mostly inert vessels, though some oak-aged examples made

grapes.name: Zinfandel/Primitivo
characteristics: Primary flavours: red fruit (strawberry, raspberry) shifting to black fruit (black plum, blackberry, blueberry) as ripeness increases; sometimes raisining giving dried fruit (prune, raisin)
Oaked: yes, in the red style, to soften tannins and add complexity
Tertiary flavours: earth, meat (old-vine California examples)
